newsitem.title: USA: Korea talks to continue in September.
newsitem.headline: Korea talks to continue in September.

text.p: The four main combatants in the 1950-53 Korean War have failed to agree on an agenda for peace negotiations after several days of talks, officials said on Thursday.
They said diplomats from the United States, China, North Korea and South Korea would meet again in September in New York to complete work on preparing details and logistics for the negotiations.
"The atmosphere of this meeting was good and we have reason to expect the same when we resume," a senior U.S. State Department official said after the three-day meetings at Columbia University.

The U.S. official and Chinese officials said diplomats from the four nations would meet again during the week of Sept. 15. They said it had been agreed that the formal negotiations would begin in Geneva four to six weeks after the end of the preparatory talks in New York.

The discussions that began on Tuesday were limited to setting a date, time, place and agenda for negotiating an arrangement to replace the armistice that ended the fighting but technically not the war on the divided Korean peninsula in 1953.

Washington and Seoul worked for more than a year to bring the Communist North Korean government to the negotiating table. U.S. officials have said it was "entirely possible" that famine-stricken North Korea was joining the talks to procure more food aid.
